thread:
sasha: quick heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion for the new starling-7b fork is hitting a subtle pretokenization mismatch. assistant messages are losing a leading space in a subset of chat templates which shifts token boundaries and our quantized runs show a small but consistent quality regression.

jordan: can you paste a minimal repro (tokenizer config + before/after tokenization)?

sasha: repro below. original HF tokenizer (works):
```json
{
  \"tokenizer_class\": \"ByteLevelBPETokenizer\",
  \"add_prefix_space\": true,
  \"normalizer\": [\"nfkc\"],
  \"byte_fallback\": false
}
```

and the converted Redwood tokenizer (current):
```json
{
  \"type\": \"byte_bpe\",
  \"pre_normalize\": false,    // <- suspect
  \"add_prefix_space\": false,
  \"keep_byte_fallback\": true
}
```

sasha: tokenization examples (HF vs Redwood):
- HF input: \"\nHello\"  => tokens: [SPACE, \"Hello\"]
- Redwood input: \"\nHello\" => tokens: [\"Hello\"]  // missing leading space token

jordan: ah — so add_prefix_space flip + pre_normalize off. That will absolutely change token alignment for chat templates where we rely on leading spaces to separate system/assistant blocks.

eli: adding context from quant runs — we ran 8-bit conversion on the converted model and saw eval delta on our standard instructions set: ROUGE-L 0.421 -> 0.409 and perplexity +5.7% on the same prompts where leading-space preservation matters. Not catastrophic but consistent.

marie: FYI this pattern also shows up in a few chat templates that start assistant replies with punctuation (\". Thanks!\"). If the tokenizer strips the implicit prefix space, the model sometimes emits a merged token which changes logits and causes weird detokenization.

tokenizer-bot: auto-diagnostic: detected mismatch in normalizer flags between HF->Redwood mapping: HF normalizer=nfkc, add_prefix_space=true -> Redwood pre_normalize should be true and add_prefix_space preserved.

jordan: short-term patch: convert with explicit flags: \`redwood-convert --hf-model path --preserve-prefix-space --force-pre-normalize\` and then re-quant. That keeps token boundaries identical.

sasha: confirmed: re-convert with those flags and re-run one quant job — ROUGE-L back to 0.420, perplexity drop close to baseline. Still want a follow-up to make converter default-safe.

eli: long-term we should add a unit test in model-onboard that runs a small suite of chat templates and asserts tokenization identity (or at least leading-space preservation) between HF tokenizer and converted tokenizer. Patch idea:
```python
# pseudo
for prompt in sample_chat_templates:
    hf_toks = hf_tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_prefix_space=True)
    rw_toks = redwood_tokenizer.encode(prompt)
    assert hf_toks == rw_toks, \"token mismatch on chat template\"
```

marie: also add a quick E2E eval in onboarding pipeline that runs quantized candidate through a 50-sample sanity set and fails the job if rouge-l drops > 0.01 absolute. Saves us from shipping subtle regressions.

sasha: filed internal ticket: ONBOARD-482 (make converter preserve normalizer and add_prefix_space by default + add regression check). tagging @jordan @eli for review.

ops-bot: rollout paused for stitch-stage:starling-7b (reason: onboarding regression alert).

jordan: I'll take ONBOARD-482. Plan: make converter map HF normalizer list -> redwood pre_normalize and preserve add_prefix_space flag, add unit tests, and add the small e2e check Marie suggested. Quick PR today.

sasha: thanks — after that we'll re-run the quant sweep and mark the earlier runs as invalid. :thumbsup:

eli: one more note — watch out for NBSP vs regular space. HF normalizers sometimes convert NBSP -> space under nfkc; if converter skips pre-normalize you'll keep NBSPs and downstream batching/prefix caching behaves differently. Add NBSP case to the test vectors.

marie: good catch. adding NBSP and leading-zero-width-space cases to sample set.

sasha: awesome. I'll attach the failing quant job logs to ONBOARD-482. For now, manual workaround is the redwood-convert flags above.

jordan: PR link when ready and I'll merge after CI.

sasha: thanks everyone.
